subject: zoology
question_text: What is cephalization? How is it useful to its possessors?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.51, VSAQ 73). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What cephalization is
steps.why: The name says it: cephalo means head, so the definition is about WHERE the nerve and sense cells lie, not how many there are.
common_mistakes: Writing that cephalization means a large brain. It is the position of the nerve and sense cells at the front end.
Placing the nerve cells at the posterior end. Cephalization is anterior.
steps.memory_tip: Cephalo means head: the nerve cells and the sense organs collect at the end that goes first.
steps.margin_note: One sentence of definition, one line on the head. Two lines are enough.
lines: Cephalization is the collecting of nerve cells
and sense organs at the anterior (front) end

steps.label: How it helps the animal
steps.why: The use follows straight from the position: the end that arrives first carries the sense organs, so the animal gets the earliest information about what is ahead.
common_mistakes: Giving only the definition. The question asks for the use as well, and that is the second mark.
steps.memory_tip: Front end first: whatever the animal meets, the head meets it before the rest of the body.
steps.margin_note: Two or three uses named. Do not write a paragraph for a 2-mark question.

lines.text: The head end meets the surroundings first

lines: The animal moves head first, so its sense
organs meet the surroundings before the rest
This helps it find food, find a mate and move

insider_note: Half the marks here are for the USE, and that is the half most students leave out — write the definition in one line and spend the rest on what cephalization does for the animal.
